stem: Healthcare workers are required to use tight-fitting respirators because of a workplace respiratory hazard. Which elements are part of the employer's OSHA respiratory protection program?

options.A: Medical evaluation, fit testing, and respirator training
options.B: Respirator distribution only, with no medical evaluation or training
options.C: Fit testing only after a worker reports a respiratory exposure
options.D: Training only, without evaluating whether the worker can medically use the respirator

rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.134 requires a written respiratory protection program for required respirator use. Applicable program elements include medical evaluation of employees required to use respirators, fit testing for tight-fitting respirators, and training on respiratory hazards and proper respirator use. Medical evaluation occurs before fit testing or required workplace use. Therefore A is correct; the other options omit required program elements or delay them until after exposure.
educational_objective: Recognize medical evaluation, fit testing, and training as core OSHA respiratory protection requirements when workers are required to use tight-fitting respirators.
source_locator: 29 CFR 1910.134(c)(1)(ii)-(iii),(vii)-(ix) Respiratory Protection Program; §1910.134(e)(1) Medical Evaluation; §1910.134(f) Fit Testing; §1910.134(k) Training and Information
source_claim_supported: When respirator use is required, OSHA requires an employer respiratory protection program that includes medical evaluation, fit testing for tight-fitting respirators, and training, among other applicable elements.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use appropriate PPE and occupational/infection-prevention practices to protect healthcare personnel
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — respiratory protection program / respirator safety
correction_summary: Specified required use of tight-fitting respirators so the full OSHA program requirements and fit-testing provisions clearly apply. Replaced the broad statement that every respirator user has identical requirements with the precise regulatory scope and removed the padded staff-member narrative.
audit_findings: A contains three directly required OSHA program elements. B and D omit mandatory components; C incorrectly delays fit testing until after exposure. The stem excludes voluntary-use ambiguity and specifies tight-fitting respirators, making fit testing directly applicable. No second answer or unresolved scope conflict remains.
